task_family_detail.feature_dtypes: all float64, no categoricals, no missing values
task_family_detail.note: classes 3 (0.58%) and 8 (1.90%) are rare; 5 and 6 hold 78.7% of mass

test_window.evidence: no date/time column in any file; no group/entity key; Id is a single contiguous integer sequence split at the boundary (train 0..2055, test 2056..3427) with identical feature schema and comparable ranges; Playground Series episodes are single-table synthetic tabular tasks with a random train/test partition. No evidence of a temporal or grouped partition.
test_window.eda_must_verify: Stage 1 must confirm no covariate shift between train and test feature distributions (adversarial validation AUC ~0.5) and check for exact duplicate feature rows across train/test (synthetic generators can emit them).

split_policy.scheme: StratifiedKFold on quality, k=5 or 10, repeated (3-5 repeats) — n=2056 makes single-shot CV noisy
split_policy.rationale: iid partition permits shuffled folds; stratification is mandatory because quality=3 has only 12 rows (a plain KFold can leave folds with zero instances of it, which breaks QWK's confusion matrix and per-fold thresholding)
split_policy.forbidden: unstratified KFold; any single 80/20 holdout for model selection at this sample size; per-fold threshold fitting evaluated on the same fold
split_policy.notes: no time-based or group-based constraint applies — no date and no entity key exists

metric.name: quadratic_weighted_kappa
traps: Not row-decomposable: QWK depends on the full predicted-label marginal distribution via the expected-agreement term, so it cannot be averaged meaningfully per row and small shifts in the predicted class histogram move the score.
Quadratic weights penalize squared label distance — an L2 regression head plus learned cutpoints is metric-aligned; plain multiclass cross-entropy (argmax decoding) is not.
Blending must happen on the continuous pre-rounding scale; averaging rounded integer labels is not a valid blend under QWK.
Rounding/cutpoint search must live INSIDE the scoring function so every CV fold and every blend candidate is evaluated post-rounding (tree-search v2 postprocessing-in-metric rule).
Cutpoints fitted per fold and scored on the same fold are optimistically biased; fit them once on the pooled OOF vector, or nested.
Rare classes 3 and 8 make the metric high-variance: whether a handful of extreme rows land in the tail class can swing QWK by a nontrivial margin. Report CV mean and spread, not a single number.
Public LB is a small slice of 1372 test rows — treat LB-vs-CV gaps as noise unless large.

external_data.reason: config.yaml special_rules.external_data_allowed = false, and pretrained_models_allowed = false / internet_access_allowed = false. Independently, the target is a physicochemical wine sensory score with no country/date/entity join key present in the data, so no whitelist source (World Bank, holiday calendars, ISO tables, ECB FX, OWID COVID) has a joinable key here.

data_level: Derived chemistry ratios from official columns only: bound SO2 = total - free sulfur dioxide; free/total SO2 ratio; fixed/volatile acidity ratio; total acidity = fixed + volatile + citric; sulphates/chlorides.
Alcohol-density interaction (alcohol and density are physically coupled through sugar/ethanol content): alcohol*density, alcohol/density, and density residual after regressing on alcohol.

Log1p transforms for right-skewed columns (residual sugar max 14.0 vs median 2.2; chlorides max 0.414 vs median 0.079; sulphates max 1.95 vs median 0.61) for the linear/kernel members; leave raw for GBDT.
Rank/quantile-transform copies of all 11 features as an alternate view for a decorrelating member.

Duplicate-row grouping: synthetic Playground data often repeats near-identical feature vectors; a within-train nearest-neighbour target-agreement feature (CV-safe, computed out-of-fold) is a candidate — verify duplicate structure in Stage 1 first (train had 0 exact feature-duplicates, so this may not fire).
model_level: Primary head: GBDT regression with L2 objective (LightGBM / XGBoost / CatBoost) on the integer target, decoded via searched cutpoints — quadratic weighting makes squared error the aligned surrogate.
Optimized cutpoint search (Nelder-Mead / coordinate scan over 5 boundaries) fitted on pooled OOF predictions, applied unchanged to test.
Diverse second head: multiclass GBDT decoded by expected value sum_k k*p_k (continuous, QWK-aligned) rather than argmax — gives blend diversity without leaving the ordinal scale.
Ordinal-specific head: cumulative-link / OrdinalClassifier (chain of binary 'quality > k' models), decoded to an expected label.

TASK-BLEND-DECOR: once the pool is built, if it is dominated by deep GBDTs, add one shallow heavily-regularized member from a different library (regularized linear / kernel ridge / small ExtraTrees on rank-transformed features) as a decorrelator, then re-optimize weights; verify weights with NNLS on the continuous scale before rounding.
Small-n discipline: heavy regularization, low learning rate with many rounds, and repeated CV for every selection decision — 2056 rows will happily support an overfit ranking.
Do NOT apply the TASK-MAE-METRIC L1-objective action here; that entry's rounding-inside-metric sub-rule transfers, its L1 objective does not (QWK is quadratic, not absolute, in label distance).

partial_task_prior_matches.why: Trigger is MAE/SMAPE/quantile-like; QWK is none of those. Its action 'rounding/threshold post-processing inside the metric function so every blend candidate sees it' transfers exactly to QWK cutpoint decoding. Its 'L1 objective not L2' action does NOT transfer — quadratic weights make L2 the aligned surrogate.

Trigger is a property of the blend pool, unknowable at Stage 0.5. Flagged for Stage 5: if the pool ends up variance-dominated (deep GBDTs), add the shallow regularized decorrelator and re-fit weights with NNLS on the continuous scale.

Trigger is a binary target with positive rate <= 2%. Target here is 6-class ordinal, but classes 3 (0.58%) and 8 (1.90%) sit in that regime. Adopt: stratified folds (already mandated by split_policy). Do not adopt resampling — QWK is an agreement metric on integer labels, and resampling distorts the predicted-marginal that QWK's expected-agreement term depends on. Entry is [GEN]/unvalidated anyway.
